column3: The Hebrew leaves the object of loving unexpressed and then names the LORD as hearer; BSB supplies the LORD as the object of love.
The Hebrew says in my days and leaves the object of calling unspecified; BSB says on Him as long as I live.
The Hebrew repeats finding: Sheol’s distresses found him and he found trouble and sorrow; BSB describes overcoming and confrontation.
The Hebrew has singular eye, tear, and foot; BSB has eyes, tears, and feet.
The Hebrew has lands in the plural; BSB has land.
The Hebrew connects believing and speaking without an explicit therefore; BSB supplies therefore.
The Hebrew names haste and a singular human lying; BSB says alarm and plural men as liars.
The Hebrew has plural benefits or recompenses; BSB says goodness.
The Hebrew has salvations in the plural; BSB has salvation.
The Hebrew speaks of loosening his bonds; BSB says breaking them.
